surprises: ⛔ CERT-7 -- MY THIRD MEASUREMENT DEFECT IN THREE PAGES, AND I COMMITTED IT IN THE RUN WHOSE OWN CONSTRAINT LIST CONTAINS K10, THE RULE AGAINST IT. mac.02's locator read 'a 7-second span, 1-7s AFTER mac.01'. Measured untruncated the family spans TEN seconds (05:26:01-05:26:10) and STARTS ONE SECOND BEFORE mac.01, bracketing rather than trailing it. MECHANISM, worse than a plain truncation: my command was `uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5`, which ranks by FREQUENCY -- I read a SPAN off a FREQUENCY RANKING and the boundary seconds were the least-populated rows, exactly what head -5 cut. A wrong domain stacked on a truncation.

The correction STRENGTHENED the conclusion for the third consecutive time (a family bracketing its sibling across ten seconds is better evidence of one emission than one trailing it across seven). I record that as LUCK, NOT METHOD: the same error class could as easily have inflated a claim with identical detectability, and I will not bank 'it always under-claims' as a property.

RESPONSE TO THE PATTERN WAS A GUARD, NOT A FOURTH RULE: enumerate_set.py, committed on my lane, makes the enumeration an ARTIFACT -- full set to a file, every figure derived from the file, distributions sorted BY KEY not by frequency, and the printed denominator carrying its set's path. Its self-test EXERCISES the failure it was built for and reproduces CERT-7 exactly. CTO~Z has since made it required equipment for W3.

The pre-filed prediction's P2 FAILURE was worth more than its two confirmations: it narrowed the predicate to binding-surface-bearing artifacts AND surfaced a second defect class (two of four entities display no as-of date anywhere) that the footer-family ticket would not have reached. Had P2 confirmed I would have counted two mis-bindings, closed the page, and never separated 'wrong date shown' from 'no date shown'.
